title: How we tracked down a 16-year-old SQLite bug
content_html:
At the end of last year, our uptime was pretty shaky. You can see this trend on our status page, and that instability continued into the new year. Many of these outages were caused by a single bug, deep in SQLite. It took months of intense forensics to track it down.

Now we’re in summer, we’re confident that we’ve found the bug, that we understand it—and more importantly, that we’ve fixed it.

We know our customers expect Tailscale to be a reliable service, and for several months we didn’t live up to that promise. That’s disruptive, and we’re sorry. We’re publishing this blog post to explain what went wrong, how we responded, and how we ultimately helped to uncover a long-standing bug in the heart of the SQLite database.

Tailscale’s database architecture

While our clients interact with our control plane as a single public endpoint (controlplane.tailscale.com), internally, our control plane is split into a series of coordination servers (or “shards”). Each tailnet lives on one internal shard at a time, but can migrate seamlessly from one to another. These shards are an internal implementation detail: you don’t know what shard your tailnet is on, and you never need to.

Each shard has an SQLite database that holds all the information about the tailnets on that shard. A single Go process exclusively accesses that database, and serves the control plane for those tailnets. This single-writer design is exactly how SQLite is meant to be used.

We’ve used SQLite as our primary database since 2022, and we chose it because it's well-known, reliable, and widely used. SQLite is “boring technology”—in a good way. Many companies use SQLite in much larger deployments without issue, and we expected the same stress-free usage.

In our current backup pipeline, we take a complete snapshot of the database every few minutes, then upload the entire SQLite file to an S3 bucket. We’d been running this setup without incident since early 2023.

Fast forward to August last year, when a data pipeline that reads those S3 backups reported an error in one of our databases. We ran SQLite’s PRAGMA integrity_check command against the backup, and found it was indeed corrupted. SQLite corruption is possible, but it’s highly unusual and not something you should encounter in normal operation. We repaired the affected database, and investigated the cause, but to no avail.

When operating at scale, even rare events can occur with some frequency, so we should have been unsurprised when it happened again—and again, and again, and again. In total, we faced 19 separate instances of database corruption over six months before we finally resolved the underlying bug.

When you hear the phrase “database corruption”, it’s natural to worry about data loss. Because our control plane only handles configuration data, these databases contain metadata about your tailnet and devices, but never your private encryption keys or network traffic. In the earliest incidents, the recovery process meant a handful of newly added devices or configuration changes didn’t persist, and a small amount of metadata had to be re-entered.

Whenever corruption occurred, we had to stop the control plane process on the shard while we repaired or restored the database. This was painful for tailnets on that shard, because their entire control plane disappeared during that recovery window. In the early incidents, that downtime was over an hour, but we gradually sped up the recovery process over subsequent incidents.

Each tailnet is a mesh network, where devices make peer-to-peer WireGuard® connections to each other. When a device joins the tailnet, it has to get a list of other devices from the control plane before it can establish new connections—so if a device came online during the SQLite downtime, it couldn’t connect. While the database was being repaired, devices already online remained connected to each other, but they couldn’t learn about changes to the network. Those tailnets also temporarily lost access to the web-based admin console and the Tailscale API.

There’s also a broader impact on trust. We post a global incident on our status page even when only a small number of tailnets are affected. Many people saw a status page event for an incident that didn’t affect them. Indeed, the majority of shards and tailnets were never involved in a database corruption incident! Nonetheless, repeated downtime erodes trust, whether or not you’re directly affected.

From the very first instance of corruption, we knew this was a serious threat to our reliability, and we threw a lot of engineering time at the problem—but the fix wasn’t easy.

Trying to find the fault

This bug resisted all our initial attempts to find it.

We looked at recent changes, but there weren’t any that seemed relevant. Nobody had been working on our low-level code that interacts with SQLite, because it had all been written years ago and presented no issues up until that point. We re-reviewed all of that code with a fine-toothed comb to look for previously missed bugs, but we didn’t find anything that would cause the corruption we were seeing.

We looked for common factors between corruption incidents, but we couldn’t find any. It wasn’t tied to a single shard, or customer, or tailnet feature, or time of day, or load level. We were at a loss for what might be triggering the behaviour.

This lack of reliable trigger conditions meant we couldn’t reproduce the bug synthetically. Instead, we had to rely on deploying passive, forensic telemetry in our live environment to catch the corruption red-handed. Gathering live diagnostics for a database issue is the last thing we wanted to do, but we had no choice.

As an additional complication, the corruption didn’t occur on a regular schedule. Sometimes incidents would be hours apart, other times weeks. This made it difficult to predict progress or plan further work, because we were never sure when we’d get our next diagnostic dump. We had a six-week period between October and December when there were no corruption incidents, before they returned as an unwelcome Christmas present.

Because this wouldn’t be a quick or easy fix, we reached out to the SQLite developers for a professional support contract. This was a great decision. It gave us direct access to their deep expertise and experience, and we had many detailed technical conversations about our architecture and our incidents.

Between Tailscale engineering and the SQLite core developers, we mapped out several theories for what might be causing the corruption—including broken POSIX locks on close(), mismanaging memory owned by SQLite, or accidentally using SQLite from multiple threads while disabling thread safety. After every incident, we gathered more data, added more diagnostics, and systematically ruled out these theories. We were gradually converging on the true bug.

The transactions that didn’t bark

While we were investigating the root cause, we still had a live platform to run. We took aggressive steps to automate recovery and minimize downtime:

  • Configuring our control plane shards to hard-stop immediately upon encountering corruption
  • Deploying an automated backup monitor that continuously ran PRAGMA integrity_check over our backups
  • Improving our runbooks and on-call training

These efforts cut our response time to under an hour—and then we discovered an unexpected clue.

We wanted a way to restore service that didn’t involve rolling back to the last known-good backup (which would lose a lot of data) or repairing the known-corrupted database (which was potentially risky).

To do this, we built a transaction logging pipeline. We streamed every SQL statement that modified the database to a separate log file. Because SQLite is a single-writer database with serialisable transactions, our transaction history was completely linear and deterministic. (This wouldn’t be true in a multi-writer database like Postgres or MySQL.) Replaying those transactions against the latest known-good backup should restore the database to its most recent state, safely bypassing the corruption.

This pipeline worked, but then it did something even better: it gave us a clue.

In two incidents, our transaction logs failed to replay cleanly. Upon closer inspection, we discovered that data written and committed by one transaction was inexplicably invisible to later transactions. A write had vanished into thin air without raising an error. That should be impossible!

The writing on the WAL

As these incidents were ongoing, the SQLite developers had been developing a new debugging tool. For a while, we’d suspected that the bug was somewhere in the checkpoint process. They were building a new tool to give better visibility into what was happening during checkpoints.

To understand what this tool found, we need to briefly explain how SQLite checkpoints work.

A SQLite database is made of a series of “pages”, tiny blocks of information. When you update the database, some of those pages need to be replaced with new pages with the updated information.

For better performance and greater concurrency, we run SQLite with Write-Ahead Logging, which means new pages aren't written directly to the database file. Instead, they’re written to the "write-ahead log" or "WAL file".

New pages can't be written to the WAL file indefinitely; at some point they have to be copied back to the main database file. This process is called “checkpointing”.

In most deployments, SQLite itself decides when to do a checkpoint, and the process is invisible to the end user and developer. In our control plane, we take manual control of the checkpoint process so we can run fast and consistent backups. This non-standard approach seemed suspicious as we steadily eliminated potential causes.

One clue was that during corruption incidents, our metrics showed that SQLite would report copying more pages from the WAL file than were actually available. If there are 10 pages in the WAL file and 20 pages get copied to the database, something is clearly wrong.

To understand what was happening during these faulty checkpoints, the SQLite developers created a new debugging tool for the virtual filesystem layer.

SQLite is split into several layers. The top layer is the parser and code generator, which converts SQL statements into SQLite’s internal data structures. These data structures get passed to the pager, which splits them into the individual pages to be written to disk. Actually writing them to disk is handled by the OS interface, or “virtual filesystem”. Currently SQLite has two mainstream virtual filesystem implementations—Unix and Windows.

If you're interested in a deeper dive on these internals, I recommend this lecture by Richard Hipp, the primary author of SQLite.

This approach allows you to replace different layers with different implementations, or wrap an existing layer to get more information. To help diagnose our problem, the SQLite developers created a wrapper around the virtual filesystem that writes additional tracing information and logs about changes to the database. This wrapper is called the tmstmpvfs shim, and the source code is available in the SQLite public repository.

We deployed the shim into our live environment, and waited for the next corruption to occur. Fortunately, we didn't have to wait long.

The WAL-Reset bug

After our next corruption incident, the additional logs from the new tmstmpvfs shim allowed the SQLite developers to find and fix the bug: a rare data race in the SQLite source code between a checkpoint and a write transaction.

In particular, if a write occurs at a specific time during a checkpoint, the checkpointing process gets confused—it thinks some of the pages have been copied from the WAL into the main database file, but they haven’t. Those pages never get written to the database file, and that data is permanently lost. The database file becomes corrupt, because other pages which reference those pages—such as an index—are written to the database.

The SQLite developers named this the “WAL-Reset bug”, and they estimate it was present in SQLite for at least 16 years. It could exist that long because it was rare—so rare, the SQLite developers had to add code to deliberately trigger it in their testing environments. Their fix adds an additional check to the checkpointing function which detects when the WAL has been reset by another thread.

They confirmed that this bug caused all of the baffling behaviour we’d seen. It explained the corruption, the transaction logs that wouldn’t apply cleanly, and the inconsistent checkpoint statistics. They also explained why we were more likely to hit the bug than other SQLite users: we take manual control of the checkpointing process, and we checkpoint very aggressively. Even a bug triggered by a rare condition was bound to hit us eventually.

This was an exciting moment. After months of confusion and uncertainty, we finally had a plausible theory for why the corruption was occurring, and a fix we could deploy to prevent it.

The SQLite developers released the fix as SQLite 3.52.0, and we prepared to deploy it as soon as it was available.

Fixed, with a false alarm

We rolled out SQLite 3.52.0 carefully—first to a few canary shards, then, when we saw it running smoothly, we deployed it to the rest of the control plane.

Our backup monitor promptly turned red, and reported corruption in 13 different databases. This was extremely alarming, but we followed our recovery procedures to fix all the supposed corruption, and everything was happy. It turned out these databases had not suffered real corruption, but were subject to a second problem in the version of SQLite.

We shared our errors with the SQLite developers, which uncovered a bug in SQLite related to stale expression indexes. If you create an index on a computed value, and then the computation changes, the index will contain mismatched values, which gets reported as corruption by PRAGMA integrity_check.

In our case, we were storing some high-precision timestamps as text, converting them to a floating-point number in a VIRTUAL generated column, and the SQLite 3.52.0 release that fixed our data race also made an optimisation that subtly changed the rounding behaviour for text-to-floating-point conversions. Our canary shards didn’t have any timestamps that triggered the changed rounding behaviour, so we missed this in our phased rollout.

Because this change caused false corruption warnings, the SQLite developers withdrew the 3.52.0 release and instead published 3.51.3, which only contained a fix for the WAL-Reset bug.

We fixed the issue on our side by reducing the precision of our timestamps to integer seconds; text-to-integer conversions are unambiguous. Meanwhile, the SQLite developers created an automated, self-healing index feature in 3.53.0, which prevents the stale expression index problem.

Party time!

With the fix rolled out to our entire control plane, we were ready to declare victory, but we were still cautious. An absence of corruption incidents doesn’t mean things are fixed—we’d already had one six-week period of deceptive calm.

We wanted positive proof that this data race was actively occurring in our production environment. Now that we understood the cause of the bug—a collision between a write transaction and a WAL-reset—we patched our SQLite driver to log a warning when these two operations overlap. If the warning fired but the database remained uncorrupted, we’d know the fix had saved us from a potential corruption incident.

We deployed the warning, and we waited. And we waited. And waited. And waited. As weeks slipped by, we began to wonder why we didn’t see it. Was the warning broken? Was our theory wrong? Was the true bug still lurking in the darkness?

Then, two months later, the alert we were waiting for finally fired:

This alert proved that the precise conditions for the WAL-Reset bug do occur in our production environment, which means it was the likely culprit for our six months of shaky uptime.

Since that weirdly joyous alert fired, we’ve run for another four months without any database incidents, as of this writing. Finally, we could breathe a sigh of relief.

Off the well-trodden path

Nobody wanted us to spend six months looking for bugs in SQLite. This was an immensely frustrating experience for both our customers and staff, and we’re all glad to put this instability behind us.

This investigation is a useful reminder: running boring technology in a non-standard way is a risk. The common paths and standard configurations are incredibly well-tested and reliable. Most people use SQLite in a standard configuration and never face this sort of issue. Everything we were doing was a public, documented, supported configuration—but by taking manual control of the checkpointing process and running at our own aggressive pace, we stepped off the well-trodden operational path.

Resolving these incidents was a massive, cross-functional effort involving dozens of people—including Tailscale's engineering and support teams, and the core maintainers of SQLite. It is to all of their credit that the impact of these incidents was not much worse.

We know that repeated downtime erodes trust, no matter how many people are affected, and we’re grateful to our customers for their patience and support while we chased this down.

Frustrating as this period was, we’re left in a stronger position than we were before. The long-standing bug in SQLite has been patched, and we fixed dozens of other incidental issues that we spotted while looking for it. We funded the open-source SQLite VFS shim that helped isolate the race condition almost immediately, and will help track down similar bugs in the future. Finally, we’ve refined our database backup and recovery processes, and live-tested them over a dozen times.

Hopefully there won’t be another database incident like this—but if there is, we’ll be ready.

sentences.en: It took months of intense forensics to track it down.
sentences.zh: 经过数月的紧张取证才找到它。

blocks.html_en: Now we’re in summer, we’re confident that we’ve found the bug, that we understand it—and more importantly, that we’ve fixed it.

sentences.en: Now we’re in summer, we’re confident that we’ve found the bug, that we understand it—and more importantly, that we’ve fixed it.
sentences.zh: 现在正值夏天，我们相信我们已经找到了这个错误，我们理解了它，更重要的是，我们已经修复了它。

blocks.html_en: We know our customers expect Tailscale to be a reliable service, and for several months we didn’t live up to that promise. That’s disruptive, and we’re sorry. We’re publishing this blog post to explain what went wrong, how we responded, and how we ultimately helped to uncover a long-standing bug in the heart of the SQLite database.

sentences.en: We know our customers expect Tailscale to be a reliable service, and for several months we didn’t live up to that promise.
sentences.zh: 我们知道我们的客户希望 Tailscale 提供可靠的服务，但几个月来我们并没有兑现这一承诺。

sentences.en: That’s disruptive, and we’re sorry.
sentences.zh: 这具有破坏性，我们很抱歉。

sentences.en: We’re publishing this blog post to explain what went wrong, how we responded, and how we ultimately helped to uncover a long-standing bug in the heart of the SQLite database.
sentences.zh: 我们发布这篇博文是为了解释出了什么问题、我们如何应对，以及我们如何最终帮助发现 SQLite 数据库核心中长期存在的错误。

blocks.html_en: Tailscale’s database architecture

sentences.en: Tailscale’s database architecture
sentences.zh: Tailscale的数据库架构

blocks.html_en: While our clients interact with our control plane as a single public endpoint (controlplane.tailscale.com), internally, our control plane is split into a series of coordination servers (or “shards”). Each tailnet lives on one internal shard at a time, but can migrate seamlessly from one to another. These shards are an internal implementation detail: you don’t know what shard your tailnet is on, and you never need to.

sentences.en: While our clients interact with our control plane as a single public endpoint (controlplane.tailscale.com), internally, our control plane is split into a series of coordination servers (or “shards”).
sentences.zh: 虽然我们的客户作为单个公共端点 (controlplane.tailscale.com) 与我们的控制平面进行交互，但在内部，我们的控制平面被分为一系列协调服务器（或“分片”）。

sentences.en: Each tailnet lives on one internal shard at a time, but can migrate seamlessly from one to another.
sentences.zh: 每个尾网一次驻留在一个内部分片上，但可以从一个分片无缝迁移到另一个分片。

sentences.en: These shards are an internal implementation detail: you don’t know what shard your tailnet is on, and you never need to.
sentences.zh: 这些分片是内部实现细节：您不知道您的尾网位于哪个分片上，而且您永远不需要知道。

blocks.html_en: Each shard has an SQLite database that holds all the information about the tailnets on that shard. A single Go process exclusively accesses that database, and serves the control plane for those tailnets. This single-writer design is exactly how SQLite is meant to be used.

sentences.en: Each shard has an SQLite database that holds all the information about the tailnets on that shard.
sentences.zh: 每个分片都有一个 SQLite 数据库，其中保存有关该分片上的 tailnets 的所有信息。

sentences.en: A single Go process exclusively accesses that database, and serves the control plane for those tailnets.
sentences.zh: 单个 Go 进程专门访问该数据库，并为这些尾网的控制平面提供服务。

sentences.en: This single-writer design is exactly how SQLite is meant to be used.
sentences.zh: 这种单写入器设计正是 SQLite 的用途。

blocks.html_en: We’ve used SQLite as our primary database since 2022, and we chose it because it's well-known, reliable, and widely used. SQLite is “boring technology”—in a good way. Many companies use SQLite in much larger deployments without issue, and we expected the same stress-free usage.

sentences.en: We’ve used SQLite as our primary database since 2022, and we chose it because it's well-known, reliable, and widely used.
sentences.zh: 自 2022 年以来，我们一直使用 SQLite 作为我们的主要数据库，我们选择它是因为它众所周知、可靠且使用广泛。

sentences.en: SQLite is “boring technology”—in a good way.
sentences.zh: SQLite 是一种“无聊的技术”——从好的方面来说。

sentences.en: Many companies use SQLite in much larger deployments without issue, and we expected the same stress-free usage.
sentences.zh: 许多公司在更大规模的部署中使用 SQLite 不会出现任何问题，我们期望同样无压力的使用。

blocks.html_en: In our current backup pipeline, we take a complete snapshot of the database every few minutes, then upload the entire SQLite file to an S3 bucket. We’d been running this setup without incident since early 2023.

sentences.en: In our current backup pipeline, we take a complete snapshot of the database every few minutes, then upload the entire SQLite file to an S3 bucket.
sentences.zh: 在我们当前的备份管道中，我们每隔几分钟拍摄一次数据库的完整快照，然后将整个 SQLite 文件上传到 S3 存储桶。

sentences.en: We’d been running this setup without incident since early 2023.
sentences.zh: 自 2023 年初以来，我们一直在运行此设置，没有发生任何事件。

blocks.html_en: Fast forward to August last year, when a data pipeline that reads those S3 backups reported an error in one of our databases. We ran SQLite’s PRAGMA integrity_check command against the backup, and found it was indeed corrupted. SQLite corruption is possible, but it’s highly unusual and not something you should encounter in normal operation. We repaired the affected database, and investigated the cause, but to no avail.

sentences.en: Fast forward to August last year, when a data pipeline that reads those S3 backups reported an error in one of our databases.
sentences.zh: 快进到去年 8 月，当时读取这些 S3 备份的数据管道报告我们的一个数据库出现错误。

sentences.en: We ran SQLite’s PRAGMA integrity_check command against the backup, and found it was indeed corrupted.
sentences.zh: 我们对备份运行 SQLite 的 PRAGMAintegrity_check 命令，发现它确实已损坏。

sentences.en: SQLite corruption is possible, but it’s highly unusual and not something you should encounter in normal operation.
sentences.zh: SQLite 损坏是可能的，但这种情况非常不寻常，不应该在正常操作中遇到。

sentences.en: We repaired the affected database, and investigated the cause, but to no avail.
sentences.zh: 我们修复了受影响的数据库，并调查了原因，但没有结果。

blocks.html_en: When operating at scale, even rare events can occur with some frequency, so we should have been unsurprised when it happened again—and again, and again, and again. In total, we faced 19 separate instances of database corruption over six months before we finally resolved the underlying bug.

sentences.en: When operating at scale, even rare events can occur with some frequency, so we should have been unsurprised when it happened again—and again, and again, and again.
sentences.zh: 当大规模运营时，即使是罕见的事件也可能以一定的频率发生，所以当它再次发生时我们应该不会感到惊讶——一次又一次，一次又一次。

sentences.en: In total, we faced 19 separate instances of database corruption over six months before we finally resolved the underlying bug.
sentences.zh: 在我们最终解决潜在错误之前的六个月内，我们总共遇到了 19 次不同的数据库损坏实例。

blocks.html_en: When you hear the phrase “database corruption”, it’s natural to worry about data loss. Because our control plane only handles configuration data, these databases contain metadata about your tailnet and devices, but never your private encryption keys or network traffic. In the earliest incidents, the recovery process meant a handful of newly added devices or configuration changes didn’t persist, and a small amount of metadata had to be re-entered.

sentences.en: When you hear the phrase “database corruption”, it’s natural to worry about data loss.
sentences.zh: 当您听到“数据库损坏”这个词时，很自然地担心数据丢失。

sentences.en: Because our control plane only handles configuration data, these databases contain metadata about your tailnet and devices, but never your private encryption keys or network traffic.
sentences.zh: 由于我们的控制平面仅处理配置数据，因此这些数据库包含有关您的尾网和设备的元数据，但绝不包含您的私有加密密钥或网络流量。

sentences.en: In the earliest incidents, the recovery process meant a handful of newly added devices or configuration changes didn’t persist, and a small amount of metadata had to be re-entered.
sentences.zh: 在最早的事件中，恢复过程意味着少数新添加的设备或配置更改不会持续存在，并且必须重新输入少量元数据。

blocks.html_en: Whenever corruption occurred, we had to stop the control plane process on the shard while we repaired or restored the database. This was painful for tailnets on that shard, because their entire control plane disappeared during that recovery window. In the early incidents, that downtime was over an hour, but we gradually sped up the recovery process over subsequent incidents.

sentences.en: Whenever corruption occurred, we had to stop the control plane process on the shard while we repaired or restored the database.
sentences.zh: 每当发生损坏时，我们就必须在修复或恢复数据库时停止分片上的控制平面进程。

sentences.en: This was painful for tailnets on that shard, because their entire control plane disappeared during that recovery window.
sentences.zh: 这对于该分片上的尾网来说是痛苦的，因为它们的整个控制平面在恢复窗口期间消失了。

sentences.en: In the early incidents, that downtime was over an hour, but we gradually sped up the recovery process over subsequent incidents.
sentences.zh: 在早期事件中，停机时间超过一个小时，但我们在后续事件中逐渐加快了恢复过程。

blocks.html_en: Each tailnet is a mesh network, where devices make peer-to-peer WireGuard® connections to each other. When a device joins the tailnet, it has to get a list of other devices from the control plane before it can establish new connections—so if a device came online during the SQLite downtime, it couldn’t connect. While the database was being repaired, devices already online remained connected to each other, but they couldn’t learn about changes to the network. Those tailnets also temporarily lost access to the web-based admin console and the Tailscale API.

sentences.en: Each tailnet is a mesh network, where devices make peer-to-peer WireGuard® connections to each other.
sentences.zh: 每个尾网都是一个网状网络，设备在其中相互建立点对点 WireGuard® 连接。

sentences.en: When a device joins the tailnet, it has to get a list of other devices from the control plane before it can establish new connections—so if a device came online during the SQLite downtime, it couldn’t connect.
sentences.zh: 当设备加入尾网时，它必须从控制平面获取其他设备的列表，然后才能建立新连接 - 因此，如果设备在 SQLite 停机期间上线，它将无法连接。

sentences.en: While the database was being repaired, devices already online remained connected to each other, but they couldn’t learn about changes to the network.
sentences.zh: 在数据库修复期间，已在线的设备仍保持相互连接，但它们无法了解网络的变化。

sentences.en: Those tailnets also temporarily lost access to the web-based admin console and the Tailscale API.
sentences.zh: 这些 tailnet 还暂时失去了对基于 Web 的管理控制台和 Tailscale API 的访问权限。

blocks.html_en: There’s also a broader impact on trust. We post a global incident on our status page even when only a small number of tailnets are affected. Many people saw a status page event for an incident that didn’t affect them. Indeed, the majority of shards and tailnets were never involved in a database corruption incident! Nonetheless, repeated downtime erodes trust, whether or not you’re directly affected.

sentences.en: There’s also a broader impact on trust.
sentences.zh: 这对信任也有更广泛的影响。

sentences.en: We post a global incident on our status page even when only a small number of tailnets are affected.
sentences.zh: 即使只有少数尾网受到影响，我们也会在状态页面上发布全球事件。

sentences.en: Many people saw a status page event for an incident that didn’t affect them.
sentences.zh: 许多人看到了对他们没有影响的事件的状态页面事件。

sentences.en: Indeed, the majority of shards and tailnets were never involved in a database corruption incident!
sentences.zh: 事实上，大多数分片和尾网从未涉及数据库损坏事件！

sentences.en: Nonetheless, repeated downtime erodes trust, whether or not you’re directly affected.
sentences.zh: 尽管如此，无论您是否受到直接影响，反复的停机都会削弱信任。

blocks.html_en: From the very first instance of corruption, we knew this was a serious threat to our reliability, and we threw a lot of engineering time at the problem—but the fix wasn’t easy.

sentences.en: From the very first instance of corruption, we knew this was a serious threat to our reliability, and we threw a lot of engineering time at the problem—but the fix wasn’t easy.
sentences.zh: 从第一次腐败事件起，我们就知道这对我们的可靠性构成严重威胁，我们投入了大量的工程时间来解决这个问题，但解决起来并不容易。

blocks.html_en: Trying to find the fault

sentences.en: Trying to find the fault
sentences.zh: 试图找出错误

blocks.html_en: This bug resisted all our initial attempts to find it.

sentences.en: This bug resisted all our initial attempts to find it.
sentences.zh: 这个错误阻止了我们最初寻找它的所有尝试。

blocks.html_en: We looked at recent changes, but there weren’t any that seemed relevant. Nobody had been working on our low-level code that interacts with SQLite, because it had all been written years ago and presented no issues up until that point. We re-reviewed all of that code with a fine-toothed comb to look for previously missed bugs, but we didn’t find anything that would cause the corruption we were seeing.

sentences.en: We looked at recent changes, but there weren’t any that seemed relevant.
sentences.zh: 我们查看了最近的变化，但没有任何看起来相关的变化。

sentences.en: Nobody had been working on our low-level code that interacts with SQLite, because it had all been written years ago and presented no issues up until that point.
sentences.zh: 没有人参与我们与 SQLite 交互的低级代码，因为它都是几年前编写的，并且在那之前没有出现任何问题。

sentences.en: We re-reviewed all of that code with a fine-toothed comb to look for previously missed bugs, but we didn’t find anything that would cause the corruption we were seeing.
sentences.zh: 我们仔细地重新审查了所有代码，以查找以前遗漏的错误，但我们没有发现任何会导致我们所看到的损坏的内容。

blocks.html_en: We looked for common factors between corruption incidents, but we couldn’t find any. It wasn’t tied to a single shard, or customer, or tailnet feature, or time of day, or load level. We were at a loss for what might be triggering the behaviour.

sentences.en: We looked for common factors between corruption incidents, but we couldn’t find any.
sentences.zh: 我们寻找腐败事件之间的共同因素，但没有找到任何共同因素。

sentences.en: It wasn’t tied to a single shard, or customer, or tailnet feature, or time of day, or load level.
sentences.zh: 它与单个分片、客户、尾网功能、一天中的时间或负载水平无关。

sentences.en: We were at a loss for what might be triggering the behaviour.
sentences.zh: 我们不知道是什么引发了这种行为。

blocks.html_en: This lack of reliable trigger conditions meant we couldn’t reproduce the bug synthetically. Instead, we had to rely on deploying passive, forensic telemetry in our live environment to catch the corruption red-handed. Gathering live diagnostics for a database issue is the last thing we wanted to do, but we had no choice.

sentences.en: This lack of reliable trigger conditions meant we couldn’t reproduce the bug synthetically.
sentences.zh: 缺乏可靠的触发条件意味着我们无法综合重现该错误。

sentences.en: Instead, we had to rely on deploying passive, forensic telemetry in our live environment to catch the corruption red-handed.
sentences.zh: 相反，我们必须依靠在我们的生活环境中部署被动的法医遥测技术来当场抓获腐败行为。

sentences.en: Gathering live diagnostics for a database issue is the last thing we wanted to do, but we had no choice.
sentences.zh: 收集数据库问题的实时诊断是我们最不想做的事情，但我们别无选择。

blocks.html_en: As an additional complication, the corruption didn’t occur on a regular schedule. Sometimes incidents would be hours apart, other times weeks. This made it difficult to predict progress or plan further work, because we were never sure when we’d get our next diagnostic dump. We had a six-week period between October and December when there were no corruption incidents, before they returned as an unwelcome Christmas present.

sentences.en: As an additional complication, the corruption didn’t occur on a regular schedule.
sentences.zh: 另一个复杂之处是，腐败行为并没有定期发生。

sentences.en: Sometimes incidents would be hours apart, other times weeks.
sentences.zh: 有时事件相隔数小时，有时则相隔数周。

sentences.en: This made it difficult to predict progress or plan further work, because we were never sure when we’d get our next diagnostic dump.
sentences.zh: 这使得预测进展或计划进一步的工作变得困难，因为我们永远不确定何时会得到下一个诊断转储。

sentences.en: We had a six-week period between October and December when there were no corruption incidents, before they returned as an unwelcome Christmas present.
sentences.zh: 10 月到 12 月之间有六周的时间没有发生腐败事件，但腐败事件却作为不受欢迎的圣诞礼物卷土重来。

blocks.html_en: Because this wouldn’t be a quick or easy fix, we reached out to the SQLite developers for a professional support contract. This was a great decision. It gave us direct access to their deep expertise and experience, and we had many detailed technical conversations about our architecture and our incidents.

sentences.en: Because this wouldn’t be a quick or easy fix, we reached out to the SQLite developers for a professional support contract.
sentences.zh: 由于这不是一个快速或简单的解决方案，因此我们联系了 SQLite 开发人员以获得专业支持合同。

sentences.en: This was a great decision.
sentences.zh: 这是一个伟大的决定。

sentences.en: It gave us direct access to their deep expertise and experience, and we had many detailed technical conversations about our architecture and our incidents.
sentences.zh: 它使我们能够直接接触到他们深厚的专业知识和经验，并且我们就我们的架构和事件进行了许多详细的技术对话。

blocks.html_en: Between Tailscale engineering and the SQLite core developers, we mapped out several theories for what might be causing the corruption—including broken POSIX locks on close(), mismanaging memory owned by SQLite, or accidentally using SQLite from multiple threads while disabling thread safety. After every incident, we gathered more data, added more diagnostics, and systematically ruled out these theories. We were gradually converging on the true bug.

sentences.en: Between Tailscale engineering and the SQLite core developers, we mapped out several theories for what might be causing the corruption—including broken POSIX locks on close(), mismanaging memory owned by SQLite, or accidentally using SQLite from multiple threads while disabling thread safety.
sentences.zh: 在 Tailscale 工程和 SQLite 核心开发人员之间，我们针对可能导致损坏的原因制定了几种理论，包括 close() 上的 POSIX 锁被破坏、SQLite 拥有的内存管理不善，或者在禁用线程安全时意外地从多个线程使用 SQLite。

sentences.en: After every incident, we gathered more data, added more diagnostics, and systematically ruled out these theories.
sentences.zh: 每次事件发生后，我们都会收集更多数据，添加更多诊断，并系统地排除这些理论。

sentences.en: We were gradually converging on the true bug.
sentences.zh: 我们逐渐接近真正的错误。

blocks.html_en: The transactions that didn’t bark

sentences.en: The transactions that didn’t bark
sentences.zh: 没有吠叫的交易

blocks.html_en: While we were investigating the root cause, we still had a live platform to run. We took aggressive steps to automate recovery and minimize downtime:

sentences.en: While we were investigating the root cause, we still had a live platform to run.
sentences.zh: 当我们调查根本原因时，我们仍然有一个实时平台可以运行。

sentences.en: We took aggressive steps to automate recovery and minimize downtime:
sentences.zh: 我们采取了积极的措施来实现恢复自动化并最大限度地减少停机时间：

blocks.html_en: • Configuring our control plane shards to hard-stop immediately upon encountering corruption

sentences.en: Configuring our control plane shards to hard-stop immediately upon encountering corruption
sentences.zh: 将我们的控制平面分片配置为在遇到损坏时立即硬停止

blocks.html_en: • Deploying an automated backup monitor that continuously ran PRAGMA integrity_check over our backups

sentences.en: Deploying an automated backup monitor that continuously ran PRAGMA integrity_check over our backups
sentences.zh: 部署自动备份监视器，对我们的备份持续运行 PRAGMAintegrity_check

blocks.html_en: • Improving our runbooks and on-call training

sentences.en: Improving our runbooks and on-call training
sentences.zh: 改进我们的操作手册和随叫随到的培训

blocks.html_en: These efforts cut our response time to under an hour—and then we discovered an unexpected clue.

sentences.en: These efforts cut our response time to under an hour—and then we discovered an unexpected clue.
sentences.zh: 这些努力将我们的响应时间缩短到不到一个小时，然后我们发现了一条意想不到的线索。

blocks.html_en: We wanted a way to restore service that didn’t involve rolling back to the last known-good backup (which would lose a lot of data) or repairing the known-corrupted database (which was potentially risky).

sentences.en: We wanted a way to restore service that didn’t involve rolling back to the last known-good backup (which would lose a lot of data) or repairing the known-corrupted database (which was potentially risky).
sentences.zh: 我们想要一种恢复服务的方法，不涉及回滚到最后一个已知良好的备份（这会丢失大量数据）或修复已知损坏的数据库（这有潜在风险）。

blocks.html_en: To do this, we built a transaction logging pipeline. We streamed every SQL statement that modified the database to a separate log file. Because SQLite is a single-writer database with serialisable transactions, our transaction history was completely linear and deterministic. (This wouldn’t be true in a multi-writer database like Postgres or MySQL.) Replaying those transactions against the latest known-good backup should restore the database to its most recent state, safely bypassing the corruption.

sentences.en: To do this, we built a transaction logging pipeline.
sentences.zh: 为此，我们构建了事务日志记录管道。

sentences.en: We streamed every SQL statement that modified the database to a separate log file.
sentences.zh: 我们将修改数据库的每个 SQL 语句流式传输到单独的日志文件中。

sentences.en: Because SQLite is a single-writer database with serialisable transactions, our transaction history was completely linear and deterministic.
sentences.zh: 因为 SQLite 是一个具有可序列化事务的单写入器数据库，所以我们的事务历史是完全线性且确定的。

sentences.en: (This wouldn’t be true in a multi-writer database like Postgres or MySQL.)
sentences.zh: （在 Postgres 或 MySQL 等多写入器数据库中，情况并非如此。）

sentences.en: Replaying those transactions against the latest known-good backup should restore the database to its most recent state, safely bypassing the corruption.
sentences.zh: 根据最新的已知良好备份重播这些事务应该将数据库恢复到最新状态，安全地绕过损坏。

blocks.html_en: This pipeline worked, but then it did something even better: it gave us a clue.

sentences.en: This pipeline worked, but then it did something even better: it gave us a clue.
sentences.zh: 这条管道奏效了，但后来它做了更好的事情：它给了我们一条线索。

blocks.html_en: In two incidents, our transaction logs failed to replay cleanly. Upon closer inspection, we discovered that data written and committed by one transaction was inexplicably invisible to later transactions. A write had vanished into thin air without raising an error. That should be impossible!

sentences.en: In two incidents, our transaction logs failed to replay cleanly.
sentences.zh: 在两次事件中，我们的事务日志未能清晰地重放。

sentences.en: Upon closer inspection, we discovered that data written and committed by one transaction was inexplicably invisible to later transactions.
sentences.zh: 经过仔细检查，我们发现一笔事务写入和提交的数据对于后续事务来说莫名其妙地不可见。

sentences.en: A write had vanished into thin air without raising an error.
sentences.zh: 一次写入就消失得无影无踪，没有引发任何错误。

sentences.en: That should be impossible!
sentences.zh: 那应该是不可能的吧！

blocks.html_en: The writing on the WAL

sentences.en: The writing on the WAL
sentences.zh: WAL 上的文字

blocks.html_en: As these incidents were ongoing, the SQLite developers had been developing a new debugging tool. For a while, we’d suspected that the bug was somewhere in the checkpoint process. They were building a new tool to give better visibility into what was happening during checkpoints.

sentences.en: As these incidents were ongoing, the SQLite developers had been developing a new debugging tool.
sentences.zh: 随着这些事件的发生，SQLite 开发人员一直在开发一种新的调试工具。

sentences.en: For a while, we’d suspected that the bug was somewhere in the checkpoint process.
sentences.zh: 有一段时间，我们怀疑这个错误是在检查点进程中的某个地方。

sentences.en: They were building a new tool to give better visibility into what was happening during checkpoints.
sentences.zh: 他们正在构建一种新工具，以便更好地了解检查站期间发生的情况。

blocks.html_en: To understand what this tool found, we need to briefly explain how SQLite checkpoints work.

sentences.en: To understand what this tool found, we need to briefly explain how SQLite checkpoints work.
sentences.zh: 为了了解这个工具发现了什么，我们需要简要解释一下 SQLite 检查点的工作原理。

blocks.html_en: A SQLite database is made of a series of “pages”, tiny blocks of information. When you update the database, some of those pages need to be replaced with new pages with the updated information.

sentences.en: A SQLite database is made of a series of “pages”, tiny blocks of information.
sentences.zh: SQLite 数据库由一系列“页面”（微小的信息块）组成。

sentences.en: When you update the database, some of those pages need to be replaced with new pages with the updated information.
sentences.zh: 当您更新数据库时，其中一些页面需要替换为包含更新信息的新页面。

blocks.html_en: For better performance and greater concurrency, we run SQLite with Write-Ahead Logging, which means new pages aren't written directly to the database file. Instead, they’re written to the "write-ahead log" or "WAL file".

sentences.en: For better performance and greater concurrency, we run SQLite with Write-Ahead Logging, which means new pages aren't written directly to the database file.
sentences.zh: 为了获得更好的性能和更大的并发性，我们运行带有预写日志记录的 SQLite，这意味着新页面不会直接写入数据库文件。

sentences.en: Instead, they’re written to the "write-ahead log" or "WAL file".
sentences.zh: 相反，它们被写入“预写日志”或“WAL 文件”。

blocks.html_en: New pages can't be written to the WAL file indefinitely; at some point they have to be copied back to the main database file. This process is called “checkpointing”.

sentences.en: New pages can't be written to the WAL file indefinitely; at some point they have to be copied back to the main database file.
sentences.zh: 新页面不能无限期地写入WAL文件；在某些时候，它们必须被复制回主数据库文件。

sentences.en: This process is called “checkpointing”.
sentences.zh: 这个过程称为“检查点”。

blocks.html_en: In most deployments, SQLite itself decides when to do a checkpoint, and the process is invisible to the end user and developer. In our control plane, we take manual control of the checkpoint process so we can run fast and consistent backups. This non-standard approach seemed suspicious as we steadily eliminated potential causes.

sentences.en: In most deployments, SQLite itself decides when to do a checkpoint, and the process is invisible to the end user and developer.
sentences.zh: 在大多数部署中，SQLite 本身决定何时执行检查点，并且该过程对最终用户和开发人员来说是不可见的。

sentences.en: In our control plane, we take manual control of the checkpoint process so we can run fast and consistent backups.
sentences.zh: 在我们的控制平面中，我们手动控制检查点过程，以便我们可以运行快速且一致的备份。

sentences.en: This non-standard approach seemed suspicious as we steadily eliminated potential causes.
sentences.zh: 当我们稳步消除潜在原因时，这种非标准方法似乎很可疑。

blocks.html_en: One clue was that during corruption incidents, our metrics showed that SQLite would report copying more pages from the WAL file than were actually available. If there are 10 pages in the WAL file and 20 pages get copied to the database, something is clearly wrong.

sentences.en: One clue was that during corruption incidents, our metrics showed that SQLite would report copying more pages from the WAL file than were actually available.
sentences.zh: 一条线索是，在损坏事件期间，我们的指标显示 SQLite 会报告从 WAL 文件复制的页面数量多于实际可用的页面数量。

sentences.en: If there are 10 pages in the WAL file and 20 pages get copied to the database, something is clearly wrong.
sentences.zh: 如果 WAL 文件中有 10 个页面，并且有 20 个页面被复制到数据库中，则显然出现了问题。

blocks.html_en: To understand what was happening during these faulty checkpoints, the SQLite developers created a new debugging tool for the virtual filesystem layer.

sentences.en: To understand what was happening during these faulty checkpoints, the SQLite developers created a new debugging tool for the virtual filesystem layer.
sentences.zh: 为了了解这些错误检查点期间发生的情况，SQLite 开发人员为虚拟文件系统层创建了一个新的调试工具。

blocks.html_en: SQLite is split into several layers. The top layer is the parser and code generator, which converts SQL statements into SQLite’s internal data structures. These data structures get passed to the pager, which splits them into the individual pages to be written to disk. Actually writing them to disk is handled by the OS interface, or “virtual filesystem”. Currently SQLite has two mainstream virtual filesystem implementations—Unix and Windows.

sentences.en: SQLite is split into several layers.
sentences.zh: SQLite 分为几个层。

sentences.en: The top layer is the parser and code generator, which converts SQL statements into SQLite’s internal data structures.
sentences.zh: 最顶层是解析器和代码生成器，它将 SQL 语句转换为 SQLite 的内部数据结构。

sentences.en: These data structures get passed to the pager, which splits them into the individual pages to be written to disk.
sentences.zh: 这些数据结构被传递到分页器，分页器将它们分成要写入磁盘的各个页面。

sentences.en: Actually writing them to disk is handled by the OS interface, or “virtual filesystem”.
sentences.zh: 实际上将它们写入磁盘是由操作系统接口或“虚拟文件系统”处理的。

sentences.en: Currently SQLite has two mainstream virtual filesystem implementations—Unix and Windows.
sentences.zh: 目前SQLite有两种主流的虚拟文件系统实现——Unix和Windows。

blocks.html_en: If you're interested in a deeper dive on these internals, I recommend this lecture by Richard Hipp, the primary author of SQLite.

sentences.en: If you're interested in a deeper dive on these internals, I recommend this lecture by Richard Hipp, the primary author of SQLite.
sentences.zh: 如果您有兴趣更深入地了解这些内部原理，我推荐 SQLite 的主要作者 Richard Hipp 的演讲。

blocks.html_en: This approach allows you to replace different layers with different implementations, or wrap an existing layer to get more information. To help diagnose our problem, the SQLite developers created a wrapper around the virtual filesystem that writes additional tracing information and logs about changes to the database. This wrapper is called the tmstmpvfs shim, and the source code is available in the SQLite public repository.

sentences.en: This approach allows you to replace different layers with different implementations, or wrap an existing layer to get more information.
sentences.zh: 这种方法允许您用不同的实现替换不同的层，或者包装现有的层以获取更多信息。

sentences.en: To help diagnose our problem, the SQLite developers created a wrapper around the virtual filesystem that writes additional tracing information and logs about changes to the database.
sentences.zh: 为了帮助诊断我们的问题，SQLite 开发人员在虚拟文件系统周围创建了一个包装器，用于写入有关数据库更改的附加跟踪信息和日志。

sentences.en: This wrapper is called the tmstmpvfs shim, and the source code is available in the SQLite public repository.
sentences.zh: 该包装器称为 tmstmpvfs shim，源代码可在 SQLite 公共存储库中获取。

blocks.html_en: We deployed the shim into our live environment, and waited for the next corruption to occur. Fortunately, we didn't have to wait long.

sentences.en: We deployed the shim into our live environment, and waited for the next corruption to occur.
sentences.zh: 我们将填充程序部署到我们的实时环境中，并等待下一次损坏发生。

sentences.en: Fortunately, we didn't have to wait long.
sentences.zh: 幸运的是，我们并没有等太久。

blocks.html_en: The WAL-Reset bug

sentences.en: The WAL-Reset bug
sentences.zh: WAL 重置错误

blocks.html_en: After our next corruption incident, the additional logs from the new tmstmpvfs shim allowed the SQLite developers to find and fix the bug: a rare data race in the SQLite source code between a checkpoint and a write transaction.

sentences.en: After our next corruption incident, the additional logs from the new tmstmpvfs shim allowed the SQLite developers to find and fix the bug: a rare data race in the SQLite source code between a checkpoint and a write transaction.
sentences.zh: 在我们的下一次损坏事件之后，来自新 tmstmpvfs shim 的附加日志使 SQLite 开发人员能够找到并修复该错误：检查点和写入事务之间的 SQLite 源代码中罕见的数据竞争。

blocks.html_en: In particular, if a write occurs at a specific time during a checkpoint, the checkpointing process gets confused—it thinks some of the pages have been copied from the WAL into the main database file, but they haven’t. Those pages never get written to the database file, and that data is permanently lost. The database file becomes corrupt, because other pages which reference those pages—such as an index—are written to the database.

sentences.en: In particular, if a write occurs at a specific time during a checkpoint, the checkpointing process gets confused—it thinks some of the pages have been copied from the WAL into the main database file, but they haven’t.
sentences.zh: 特别是，如果在检查点期间的特定时间发生写入，则检查点过程会变得混乱 - 它认为某些页面已从 WAL 复制到主数据库文件中，但实际上并没有。

sentences.en: Those pages never get written to the database file, and that data is permanently lost.
sentences.zh: 这些页面永远不会写入数据库文件，并且该数据将永久丢失。

sentences.en: The database file becomes corrupt, because other pages which reference those pages—such as an index—are written to the database.
sentences.zh: 数据库文件被损坏，因为引用这些页面的其他页面（例如索引）被写入数据库。

blocks.html_en: The SQLite developers named this the “WAL-Reset bug”, and they estimate it was present in SQLite for at least 16 years. It could exist that long because it was rare—so rare, the SQLite developers had to add code to deliberately trigger it in their testing environments. Their fix adds an additional check to the checkpointing function which detects when the WAL has been reset by another thread.

sentences.en: The SQLite developers named this the “WAL-Reset bug”, and they estimate it was present in SQLite for at least 16 years.
sentences.zh: SQLite 开发人员将此称为“WAL-Reset bug”，他们估计它在 SQLite 中存在至少 16 年。

sentences.en: It could exist that long because it was rare—so rare, the SQLite developers had to add code to deliberately trigger it in their testing environments.
sentences.zh: 它之所以能够存在那么久，是因为它很罕见——如此罕见，以至于 SQLite 开发人员必须添加代码来在测试环境中故意触发它。

sentences.en: Their fix adds an additional check to the checkpointing function which detects when the WAL has been reset by another thread.
sentences.zh: 他们的修复为检查点功能添加了额外的检查，该检查功能检测 WAL 何时被另一个线程重置。

blocks.html_en: They confirmed that this bug caused all of the baffling behaviour we’d seen. It explained the corruption, the transaction logs that wouldn’t apply cleanly, and the inconsistent checkpoint statistics. They also explained why we were more likely to hit the bug than other SQLite users: we take manual control of the checkpointing process, and we checkpoint very aggressively. Even a bug triggered by a rare condition was bound to hit us eventually.

sentences.en: They confirmed that this bug caused all of the baffling behaviour we’d seen.
sentences.zh: 他们证实这个错误导致了我们所看到的所有令人困惑的行为。

sentences.en: It explained the corruption, the transaction logs that wouldn’t apply cleanly, and the inconsistent checkpoint statistics.
sentences.zh: 它解释了损坏、无法干净应用的事务日志以及不一致的检查点统计信息。

sentences.en: They also explained why we were more likely to hit the bug than other SQLite users: we take manual control of the checkpointing process, and we checkpoint very aggressively.
sentences.zh: 他们还解释了为什么我们比其他 SQLite 用户更有可能遇到该错误：我们手动控制检查点过程，并且我们非常积极地进行检查点。

sentences.en: Even a bug triggered by a rare condition was bound to hit us eventually.
sentences.zh: 即使是由罕见情况触发的错误最终也必然会袭击我们。

blocks.html_en: This was an exciting moment. After months of confusion and uncertainty, we finally had a plausible theory for why the corruption was occurring, and a fix we could deploy to prevent it.

sentences.en: This was an exciting moment.
sentences.zh: 这是一个激动人心的时刻。

sentences.en: After months of confusion and uncertainty, we finally had a plausible theory for why the corruption was occurring, and a fix we could deploy to prevent it.
sentences.zh: 经过几个月的困惑和不确定，我们终于对腐败发生的原因有了一个合理的理论，以及我们可以部署的解决方案来防止腐败。

blocks.html_en: The SQLite developers released the fix as SQLite 3.52.0, and we prepared to deploy it as soon as it was available.

sentences.en: The SQLite developers released the fix as SQLite 3.52.0, and we prepared to deploy it as soon as it was available.
sentences.zh: SQLite 开发人员将修复程序发布为 SQLite 3.52.0，我们准备在它可用后立即部署它。

blocks.html_en: Fixed, with a false alarm

sentences.en: Fixed, with a false alarm
sentences.zh: 已修复，有误报

blocks.html_en: We rolled out SQLite 3.52.0 carefully—first to a few canary shards, then, when we saw it running smoothly, we deployed it to the rest of the control plane.

sentences.en: We rolled out SQLite 3.52.0 carefully—first to a few canary shards, then, when we saw it running smoothly, we deployed it to the rest of the control plane.
sentences.zh: 我们小心地推出了 SQLite 3.52.0，首先是几个金丝雀分片，然后，当我们看到它运行顺利时，我们将其部署到控制平面的其余部分。

blocks.html_en: Our backup monitor promptly turned red, and reported corruption in 13 different databases. This was extremely alarming, but we followed our recovery procedures to fix all the supposed corruption, and everything was happy. It turned out these databases had not suffered real corruption, but were subject to a second problem in the version of SQLite.

sentences.en: Our backup monitor promptly turned red, and reported corruption in 13 different databases.
sentences.zh: 我们的备份监视器立即变成红色，并报告 13 个不同的数据库出现损坏。

sentences.en: This was extremely alarming, but we followed our recovery procedures to fix all the supposed corruption, and everything was happy.
sentences.zh: 这是非常令人震惊的，但我们按照恢复程序修复了所有所谓的损坏，一切都很顺利。

sentences.en: It turned out these databases had not suffered real corruption, but were subject to a second problem in the version of SQLite.
sentences.zh: 事实证明，这些数据库并没有遭受真正的损坏，而是遇到了 SQLite 版本中的第二个问题。

blocks.html_en: We shared our errors with the SQLite developers, which uncovered a bug in SQLite related to stale expression indexes. If you create an index on a computed value, and then the computation changes, the index will contain mismatched values, which gets reported as corruption by PRAGMA integrity_check.

sentences.en: We shared our errors with the SQLite developers, which uncovered a bug in SQLite related to stale expression indexes.
sentences.zh: 我们与 SQLite 开发人员分享了我们的错误，他们发现了 SQLite 中与过时表达式索引相关的错误。

sentences.en: If you create an index on a computed value, and then the computation changes, the index will contain mismatched values, which gets reported as corruption by PRAGMA integrity_check.
sentences.zh: 如果您在计算值上创建索引，然后计算发生更改，则索引将包含不匹配的值，PRAGMAintegrity_check 会将其报告为损坏。

blocks.html_en: In our case, we were storing some high-precision timestamps as text, converting them to a floating-point number in a VIRTUAL generated column, and the SQLite 3.52.0 release that fixed our data race also made an optimisation that subtly changed the rounding behaviour for text-to-floating-point conversions. Our canary shards didn’t have any timestamps that triggered the changed rounding behaviour, so we missed this in our phased rollout.

sentences.en: In our case, we were storing some high-precision timestamps as text, converting them to a floating-point number in a VIRTUAL generated column, and the SQLite 3.52.0 release that fixed our data race also made an optimisation that subtly changed the rounding behaviour for text-to-floating-point conversions.
sentences.zh: 在我们的例子中，我们将一些高精度时间戳存储为文本，将它们转换为虚拟生成列中的浮点数，修复了数据争用的 SQLite 3.52.0 版本还进行了优化，巧妙地改变了文本到浮点转换的舍入行为。

sentences.en: Our canary shards didn’t have any timestamps that triggered the changed rounding behaviour, so we missed this in our phased rollout.
sentences.zh: 我们的金丝雀分片没有任何触发更改舍入行为的时间戳，因此我们在分阶段推出中错过了这一点。

blocks.html_en: Because this change caused false corruption warnings, the SQLite developers withdrew the 3.52.0 release and instead published 3.51.3, which only contained a fix for the WAL-Reset bug.

sentences.en: Because this change caused false corruption warnings, the SQLite developers withdrew the 3.52.0 release and instead published 3.51.3, which only contained a fix for the WAL-Reset bug.
sentences.zh: 由于此更改导致错误的损坏警告，SQLite 开发人员撤回了 3.52.0 版本，并发布了 3.51.3，其中仅包含对 WAL-Reset 错误的修复。

blocks.html_en: We fixed the issue on our side by reducing the precision of our timestamps to integer seconds; text-to-integer conversions are unambiguous. Meanwhile, the SQLite developers created an automated, self-healing index feature in 3.53.0, which prevents the stale expression index problem.

sentences.en: We fixed the issue on our side by reducing the precision of our timestamps to integer seconds; text-to-integer conversions are unambiguous.
sentences.zh: 我们通过将时间戳的精度降低到整数秒来解决了这个问题；文本到整数的转换是明确的。

sentences.en: Meanwhile, the SQLite developers created an automated, self-healing index feature in 3.53.0, which prevents the stale expression index problem.
sentences.zh: 同时，SQLite开发人员在3.53.0中创建了一个自动化的、自我修复的索引功能，可以防止过时的表达式索引问题。

blocks.html_en: Party time!

sentences.en: Party time!
sentences.zh: 聚会时间！

blocks.html_en: With the fix rolled out to our entire control plane, we were ready to declare victory, but we were still cautious. An absence of corruption incidents doesn’t mean things are fixed—we’d already had one six-week period of deceptive calm.

sentences.en: With the fix rolled out to our entire control plane, we were ready to declare victory, but we were still cautious.
sentences.zh: 随着修复程序扩展到我们的整个控制平面，我们已经准备好宣布胜利，但我们仍然保持谨慎。

sentences.en: An absence of corruption incidents doesn’t mean things are fixed—we’d already had one six-week period of deceptive calm.
sentences.zh: 没有发生腐败事件并不意味着事情已经解决了——我们已经度过了为期六周的虚假平静期。

blocks.html_en: We wanted positive proof that this data race was actively occurring in our production environment. Now that we understood the cause of the bug—a collision between a write transaction and a WAL-reset—we patched our SQLite driver to log a warning when these two operations overlap. If the warning fired but the database remained uncorrupted, we’d know the fix had saved us from a potential corruption incident.

sentences.en: We wanted positive proof that this data race was actively occurring in our production environment.
sentences.zh: 我们需要积极的证据来证明这种数据竞争在我们的生产环境中正在积极发生。

sentences.en: Now that we understood the cause of the bug—a collision between a write transaction and a WAL-reset—we patched our SQLite driver to log a warning when these two operations overlap.
sentences.zh: 现在我们了解了 bug 的原因（写入事务和 WAL 重置之间的冲突），我们修补了 SQLite 驱动程序，以便在这两个操作重叠时记录警告。

sentences.en: If the warning fired but the database remained uncorrupted, we’d know the fix had saved us from a potential corruption incident.
sentences.zh: 如果警告发出但数据库仍未损坏，我们就知道修复已使我们免于潜在的损坏事件。

blocks.html_en: We deployed the warning, and we waited. And we waited. And waited. And waited. As weeks slipped by, we began to wonder why we didn’t see it. Was the warning broken? Was our theory wrong? Was the true bug still lurking in the darkness?

sentences.en: We deployed the warning, and we waited.
sentences.zh: 我们部署了警告，然后等待。

sentences.en: And we waited.
sentences.zh: 我们等待着。

sentences.en: And waited.
sentences.zh: 并等待着。

sentences.en: And waited.
sentences.zh: 并等待着。

sentences.en: As weeks slipped by, we began to wonder why we didn’t see it.
sentences.zh: 几周过去了，我们开始想知道为什么我们没有看到它。

sentences.en: Was the warning broken?
sentences.zh: 警告被打破了吗？

sentences.en: Was our theory wrong?
sentences.zh: 我们的理论错了吗？

sentences.en: Was the true bug still lurking in the darkness?
sentences.zh: 真正的虫子还潜伏在黑暗中吗？

blocks.html_en: Then, two months later, the alert we were waiting for finally fired:

sentences.en: Then, two months later, the alert we were waiting for finally fired:
sentences.zh: 然后，两个月后，我们等待的警报终于响起：

blocks.html_en: This alert proved that the precise conditions for the WAL-Reset bug do occur in our production environment, which means it was the likely culprit for our six months of shaky uptime.

sentences.en: This alert proved that the precise conditions for the WAL-Reset bug do occur in our production environment, which means it was the likely culprit for our six months of shaky uptime.
sentences.zh: 此警报证明，WAL-Reset 错误的精确条件确实发生在我们的生产环境中，这意味着它可能是导致我们六个月正常运行时间不稳定的罪魁祸首。

blocks.html_en: Since that weirdly joyous alert fired, we’ve run for another four months without any database incidents, as of this writing. Finally, we could breathe a sigh of relief.

sentences.en: Since that weirdly joyous alert fired, we’ve run for another four months without any database incidents, as of this writing.
sentences.zh: 自从发出那个奇怪的快乐警报以来，截至撰写本文时，我们已经运行了四个月，没有发生任何数据库事件。

sentences.en: Finally, we could breathe a sigh of relief.
sentences.zh: 终于，我们可以松一口气了。

blocks.html_en: Off the well-trodden path

sentences.en: Off the well-trodden path
sentences.zh: 远离人们常走的路

blocks.html_en: Nobody wanted us to spend six months looking for bugs in SQLite. This was an immensely frustrating experience for both our customers and staff, and we’re all glad to put this instability behind us.

sentences.en: Nobody wanted us to spend six months looking for bugs in SQLite.
sentences.zh: 没有人希望我们花六个月的时间寻找 SQLite 中的错误。

sentences.en: This was an immensely frustrating experience for both our customers and staff, and we’re all glad to put this instability behind us.
sentences.zh: 对于我们的客户和员工来说，这都是一次非常令人沮丧的经历，我们很高兴将这种不稳定抛在脑后。

blocks.html_en: This investigation is a useful reminder: running boring technology in a non-standard way is a risk. The common paths and standard configurations are incredibly well-tested and reliable. Most people use SQLite in a standard configuration and never face this sort of issue. Everything we were doing was a public, documented, supported configuration—but by taking manual control of the checkpointing process and running at our own aggressive pace, we stepped off the well-trodden operational path.

sentences.en: This investigation is a useful reminder: running boring technology in a non-standard way is a risk.
sentences.zh: 这项调查是一个有用的提醒：以非标准方式运行钻孔技术是有风险的。

sentences.en: The common paths and standard configurations are incredibly well-tested and reliable.
sentences.zh: 通用路径和标准配置经过了令人难以置信的良好测试且可靠。

sentences.en: Most people use SQLite in a standard configuration and never face this sort of issue.

content_html_zh:
去年年底，我们的正常运行时间相当不稳定。 您可以在我们的状态页面上看到这种趋势，并且这种不稳定持续到新的一年。 其中许多中断是由 SQLite 深处的一个错误引起的。 经过数月的紧张取证才找到它。

现在正值夏天，我们相信我们已经找到了这个错误，我们理解了它，更重要的是，我们已经修复了它。

我们知道我们的客户希望 Tailscale 提供可靠的服务，但几个月来我们并没有兑现这一承诺。 这具有破坏性，我们很抱歉。 我们发布这篇博文是为了解释出了什么问题、我们如何应对，以及我们如何最终帮助发现 SQLite 数据库核心中长期存在的错误。

Tailscale的数据库架构

虽然我们的客户作为单个公共端点 (controlplane.tailscale.com) 与我们的控制平面进行交互，但在内部，我们的控制平面被分为一系列协调服务器（或“分片”）。 每个尾网一次驻留在一个内部分片上，但可以从一个分片无缝迁移到另一个分片。 这些分片是内部实现细节：您不知道您的尾网位于哪个分片上，而且您永远不需要知道。

每个分片都有一个 SQLite 数据库，其中保存有关该分片上的 tailnets 的所有信息。 单个 Go 进程专门访问该数据库，并为这些尾网的控制平面提供服务。 这种单写入器设计正是 SQLite 的用途。

自 2022 年以来，我们一直使用 SQLite 作为我们的主要数据库，我们选择它是因为它众所周知、可靠且使用广泛。 SQLite 是一种“无聊的技术”——从好的方面来说。 许多公司在更大规模的部署中使用 SQLite 不会出现任何问题，我们期望同样无压力的使用。

在我们当前的备份管道中，我们每隔几分钟拍摄一次数据库的完整快照，然后将整个 SQLite 文件上传到 S3 存储桶。 自 2023 年初以来，我们一直在运行此设置，没有发生任何事件。

快进到去年 8 月，当时读取这些 S3 备份的数据管道报告我们的一个数据库出现错误。 我们对备份运行 SQLite 的 PRAGMAintegrity_check 命令，发现它确实已损坏。 SQLite 损坏是可能的，但这种情况非常不寻常，不应该在正常操作中遇到。 我们修复了受影响的数据库，并调查了原因，但没有结果。

当大规模运营时，即使是罕见的事件也可能以一定的频率发生，所以当它再次发生时我们应该不会感到惊讶——一次又一次，一次又一次。 在我们最终解决潜在错误之前的六个月内，我们总共遇到了 19 次不同的数据库损坏实例。

当您听到“数据库损坏”这个词时，很自然地担心数据丢失。 由于我们的控制平面仅处理配置数据，因此这些数据库包含有关您的尾网和设备的元数据，但绝不包含您的私有加密密钥或网络流量。 在最早的事件中，恢复过程意味着少数新添加的设备或配置更改不会持续存在，并且必须重新输入少量元数据。

每当发生损坏时，我们就必须在修复或恢复数据库时停止分片上的控制平面进程。 这对于该分片上的尾网来说是痛苦的，因为它们的整个控制平面在恢复窗口期间消失了。 在早期事件中，停机时间超过一个小时，但我们在后续事件中逐渐加快了恢复过程。

每个尾网都是一个网状网络，设备在其中相互建立点对点 WireGuard® 连接。 当设备加入尾网时，它必须从控制平面获取其他设备的列表，然后才能建立新连接 - 因此，如果设备在 SQLite 停机期间上线，它将无法连接。 在数据库修复期间，已在线的设备仍保持相互连接，但它们无法了解网络的变化。 这些 tailnet 还暂时失去了对基于 Web 的管理控制台和 Tailscale API 的访问权限。

这对信任也有更广泛的影响。 即使只有少数尾网受到影响，我们也会在状态页面上发布全球事件。 许多人看到了对他们没有影响的事件的状态页面事件。 事实上，大多数分片和尾网从未涉及数据库损坏事件！ 尽管如此，无论您是否受到直接影响，反复的停机都会削弱信任。

从第一次腐败事件起，我们就知道这对我们的可靠性构成严重威胁，我们投入了大量的工程时间来解决这个问题，但解决起来并不容易。

试图找出错误

这个错误阻止了我们最初寻找它的所有尝试。

我们查看了最近的变化，但没有任何看起来相关的变化。 没有人参与我们与 SQLite 交互的低级代码，因为它都是几年前编写的，并且在那之前没有出现任何问题。 我们仔细地重新审查了所有代码，以查找以前遗漏的错误，但我们没有发现任何会导致我们所看到的损坏的内容。

我们寻找腐败事件之间的共同因素，但没有找到任何共同因素。 它与单个分片、客户、尾网功能、一天中的时间或负载水平无关。 我们不知道是什么引发了这种行为。

缺乏可靠的触发条件意味着我们无法综合重现该错误。 相反，我们必须依靠在我们的生活环境中部署被动的法医遥测技术来当场抓获腐败行为。 收集数据库问题的实时诊断是我们最不想做的事情，但我们别无选择。

另一个复杂之处是，腐败行为并没有定期发生。 有时事件相隔数小时，有时则相隔数周。 这使得预测进展或计划进一步的工作变得困难，因为我们永远不确定何时会得到下一个诊断转储。 10 月到 12 月之间有六周的时间没有发生腐败事件，但腐败事件却作为不受欢迎的圣诞礼物卷土重来。

由于这不是一个快速或简单的解决方案，因此我们联系了 SQLite 开发人员以获得专业支持合同。 这是一个伟大的决定。 它使我们能够直接接触到他们深厚的专业知识和经验，并且我们就我们的架构和事件进行了许多详细的技术对话。

在 Tailscale 工程和 SQLite 核心开发人员之间，我们针对可能导致损坏的原因制定了几种理论，包括 close() 上的 POSIX 锁被破坏、SQLite 拥有的内存管理不善，或者在禁用线程安全时意外地从多个线程使用 SQLite。 每次事件发生后，我们都会收集更多数据，添加更多诊断，并系统地排除这些理论。 我们逐渐接近真正的错误。

没有吠叫的交易

当我们调查根本原因时，我们仍然有一个实时平台可以运行。 我们采取了积极的措施来实现恢复自动化并最大限度地减少停机时间：

  • 将我们的控制平面分片配置为在遇到损坏时立即硬停止
  • 部署自动备份监视器，对我们的备份持续运行 PRAGMAintegrity_check
  • 改进我们的操作手册和随叫随到的培训

这些努力将我们的响应时间缩短到不到一个小时，然后我们发现了一条意想不到的线索。

我们想要一种恢复服务的方法，不涉及回滚到最后一个已知良好的备份（这会丢失大量数据）或修复已知损坏的数据库（这有潜在风险）。

为此，我们构建了事务日志记录管道。 我们将修改数据库的每个 SQL 语句流式传输到单独的日志文件中。 因为 SQLite 是一个具有可序列化事务的单写入器数据库，所以我们的事务历史是完全线性且确定的。 （在 Postgres 或 MySQL 等多写入器数据库中，情况并非如此。） 根据最新的已知良好备份重播这些事务应该将数据库恢复到最新状态，安全地绕过损坏。

这条管道奏效了，但后来它做了更好的事情：它给了我们一条线索。

在两次事件中，我们的事务日志未能清晰地重放。 经过仔细检查，我们发现一笔事务写入和提交的数据对于后续事务来说莫名其妙地不可见。 一次写入就消失得无影无踪，没有引发任何错误。 那应该是不可能的吧！

WAL 上的文字

随着这些事件的发生，SQLite 开发人员一直在开发一种新的调试工具。 有一段时间，我们怀疑这个错误是在检查点进程中的某个地方。 他们正在构建一种新工具，以便更好地了解检查站期间发生的情况。

为了了解这个工具发现了什么，我们需要简要解释一下 SQLite 检查点的工作原理。

SQLite 数据库由一系列“页面”（微小的信息块）组成。 当您更新数据库时，其中一些页面需要替换为包含更新信息的新页面。

为了获得更好的性能和更大的并发性，我们运行带有预写日志记录的 SQLite，这意味着新页面不会直接写入数据库文件。 相反，它们被写入“预写日志”或“WAL 文件”。

新页面不能无限期地写入WAL文件；在某些时候，它们必须被复制回主数据库文件。 这个过程称为“检查点”。

在大多数部署中，SQLite 本身决定何时执行检查点，并且该过程对最终用户和开发人员来说是不可见的。 在我们的控制平面中，我们手动控制检查点过程，以便我们可以运行快速且一致的备份。 当我们稳步消除潜在原因时，这种非标准方法似乎很可疑。

一条线索是，在损坏事件期间，我们的指标显示 SQLite 会报告从 WAL 文件复制的页面数量多于实际可用的页面数量。 如果 WAL 文件中有 10 个页面，并且有 20 个页面被复制到数据库中，则显然出现了问题。

为了了解这些错误检查点期间发生的情况，SQLite 开发人员为虚拟文件系统层创建了一个新的调试工具。

SQLite 分为几个层。 最顶层是解析器和代码生成器，它将 SQL 语句转换为 SQLite 的内部数据结构。 这些数据结构被传递到分页器，分页器将它们分成要写入磁盘的各个页面。 实际上将它们写入磁盘是由操作系统接口或“虚拟文件系统”处理的。 目前SQLite有两种主流的虚拟文件系统实现——Unix和Windows。

如果您有兴趣更深入地了解这些内部原理，我推荐 SQLite 的主要作者 Richard Hipp 的演讲。

这种方法允许您用不同的实现替换不同的层，或者包装现有的层以获取更多信息。 为了帮助诊断我们的问题，SQLite 开发人员在虚拟文件系统周围创建了一个包装器，用于写入有关数据库更改的附加跟踪信息和日志。 该包装器称为 tmstmpvfs shim，源代码可在 SQLite 公共存储库中获取。

我们将填充程序部署到我们的实时环境中，并等待下一次损坏发生。 幸运的是，我们并没有等太久。

WAL 重置错误

在我们的下一次损坏事件之后，来自新 tmstmpvfs shim 的附加日志使 SQLite 开发人员能够找到并修复该错误：检查点和写入事务之间的 SQLite 源代码中罕见的数据竞争。

特别是，如果在检查点期间的特定时间发生写入，则检查点过程会变得混乱 - 它认为某些页面已从 WAL 复制到主数据库文件中，但实际上并没有。 这些页面永远不会写入数据库文件，并且该数据将永久丢失。 数据库文件被损坏，因为引用这些页面的其他页面（例如索引）被写入数据库。

SQLite 开发人员将此称为“WAL-Reset bug”，他们估计它在 SQLite 中存在至少 16 年。 它之所以能够存在那么久，是因为它很罕见——如此罕见，以至于 SQLite 开发人员必须添加代码来在测试环境中故意触发它。 他们的修复为检查点功能添加了额外的检查，该检查功能检测 WAL 何时被另一个线程重置。

他们证实这个错误导致了我们所看到的所有令人困惑的行为。 它解释了损坏、无法干净应用的事务日志以及不一致的检查点统计信息。 他们还解释了为什么我们比其他 SQLite 用户更有可能遇到该错误：我们手动控制检查点过程，并且我们非常积极地进行检查点。 即使是由罕见情况触发的错误最终也必然会袭击我们。

这是一个激动人心的时刻。 经过几个月的困惑和不确定，我们终于对腐败发生的原因有了一个合理的理论，以及我们可以部署的解决方案来防止腐败。

SQLite 开发人员将修复程序发布为 SQLite 3.52.0，我们准备在它可用后立即部署它。

已修复，有误报

我们小心地推出了 SQLite 3.52.0，首先是几个金丝雀分片，然后，当我们看到它运行顺利时，我们将其部署到控制平面的其余部分。

我们的备份监视器立即变成红色，并报告 13 个不同的数据库出现损坏。 这是非常令人震惊的，但我们按照恢复程序修复了所有所谓的损坏，一切都很顺利。 事实证明，这些数据库并没有遭受真正的损坏，而是遇到了 SQLite 版本中的第二个问题。

我们与 SQLite 开发人员分享了我们的错误，他们发现了 SQLite 中与过时表达式索引相关的错误。 如果您在计算值上创建索引，然后计算发生更改，则索引将包含不匹配的值，PRAGMAintegrity_check 会将其报告为损坏。

在我们的例子中，我们将一些高精度时间戳存储为文本，将它们转换为虚拟生成列中的浮点数，修复了数据争用的 SQLite 3.52.0 版本还进行了优化，巧妙地改变了文本到浮点转换的舍入行为。 我们的金丝雀分片没有任何触发更改舍入行为的时间戳，因此我们在分阶段推出中错过了这一点。

由于此更改导致错误的损坏警告，SQLite 开发人员撤回了 3.52.0 版本，并发布了 3.51.3，其中仅包含对 WAL-Reset 错误的修复。

我们通过将时间戳的精度降低到整数秒来解决了这个问题；文本到整数的转换是明确的。 同时，SQLite开发人员在3.53.0中创建了一个自动化的、自我修复的索引功能，可以防止过时的表达式索引问题。

聚会时间！

随着修复程序扩展到我们的整个控制平面，我们已经准备好宣布胜利，但我们仍然保持谨慎。 没有发生腐败事件并不意味着事情已经解决了——我们已经度过了为期六周的虚假平静期。

我们需要积极的证据来证明这种数据竞争在我们的生产环境中正在积极发生。 现在我们了解了 bug 的原因（写入事务和 WAL 重置之间的冲突），我们修补了 SQLite 驱动程序，以便在这两个操作重叠时记录警告。 如果警告发出但数据库仍未损坏，我们就知道修复已使我们免于潜在的损坏事件。

我们部署了警告，然后等待。 我们等待着。 并等待着。 并等待着。 几周过去了，我们开始想知道为什么我们没有看到它。 警告被打破了吗？ 我们的理论错了吗？ 真正的虫子还潜伏在黑暗中吗？

然后，两个月后，我们等待的警报终于响起：

此警报证明，WAL-Reset 错误的精确条件确实发生在我们的生产环境中，这意味着它可能是导致我们六个月正常运行时间不稳定的罪魁祸首。

自从发出那个奇怪的快乐警报以来，截至撰写本文时，我们已经运行了四个月，没有发生任何数据库事件。 终于，我们可以松一口气了。

远离人们常走的路

没有人希望我们花六个月的时间寻找 SQLite 中的错误。 对于我们的客户和员工来说，这都是一次非常令人沮丧的经历，我们很高兴将这种不稳定抛在脑后。

这项调查是一个有用的提醒：以非标准方式运行钻孔技术是有风险的。 通用路径和标准配置经过了令人难以置信的良好测试且可靠。 大多数人在标准配置中使用 SQLite，从来不会遇到此类问题。 我们所做的一切都是公开的、记录在案的、受支持的配置，但通过手动控制检查点过程并按照我们自己的积极节奏运行，我们走出了常见的操作路径。

解决这些事件是一项涉及数十人的大规模跨职能工作，其中包括 Tailscale 的工程和支持团队以及 SQLite 的核心维护人员。 值得赞扬的是，这些事件的影响并没有变得更严重。

我们知道，无论有多少人受到影响，反复的停机都会侵蚀信任，我们感谢客户在我们解决这一问题时所给予的耐心和支持。

尽管这一时期令人沮丧，但我们的处境比以前更有利。 SQLite 中长期存在的错误已得到修复，并且我们修复了在查找它时发现的数十个其他偶然问题。 我们资助了开源 SQLite VFS shim，它几乎立即帮助隔离了竞争条件，并将帮助将来追踪类似的错误。 最后，我们改进了数据库备份和恢复流程，并对它们进行了十几次现场测试。

希望不会再发生类似的数据库事件，但如果发生的话，我们会做好准备。
